The frontend (`attachPlots`/`proccessKnotData`) builds, per knot, rows `{<knotId>_index,<knotId>_abstract,<knotId>_highlight}`; multiple plot knots are **merged row-by-row** (must be equal length & aligned) so a scatter can reference `knotA_abstract` (x) and `knotB_abstract` (y). **`interaction:"BRUSH"` THROWS "Plot BRUSH not implemented yet"** in 0.8.9 — only `CLICK`/`HOVER` are wired to map highlight. So implement "brush points→highlight buildings" with `CLICK` (toggles per-point selection, highlights the building blue). KEY: the plot knot that drives highlight must be the **rendered** map knot (in `map.knots`), else the highlight writes to a non-rendered shader and is invisible — so make the x-knot (per-building noise, OBJECTS) BOTH the map color knot AND scatter x; the y-knot (area) is plot-only (in component `knots` but not `map.knots` — `initKnots` runs `processThematicData`+`loadShaders` for ALL component knots regardless). One point per building ⇒ knots at **OBJECTS** level: buildings supports an OBJECTS abstract join (`getAbstractDataFromLink` OBJECTS branch expands each object's single `inValue` across its vertices via `getCoordsPerComp`; `inValues` length must == #buildings = #mesh components). Put MULTIPLE joins in one `buildings_joined.json` (`joinedLayers[]`+`joinedObjects[]`), matched by (`layerId`==in.name, inLevel, outLevel, spatial_relation, abstract). Building **area**: shoelace on `sectionFootprint[0]` reprojected 3395→32618 (3395 area distorted ~1.74× at 40.7°). Live `utk start --data ./data` validates fine under `timeout` (routes `/getGrammar`,`/getLayer?layer=`,`/files/*` all 200) — but watch for a **stale prior utk server holding :5001** ("Address already in use"): `ss -ltnp|grep 5001` then `kill`.

To get aligned lengths: **monkeypatch `OSM.osm_to_roads_polyline`** to re-derive `inter_parts` from the same `osm_elements`/`bpoly` (deterministic same order as the mesh — verified `len(centerlines)==len(mesh.data)`, 20642 for full island) and measure each `LineString` in EPSG:32618 (true metres; 3395 length inflated ~1.32×). Colour roads by length via an **OBJECTS abstract NEAREST join** (one value/road, like the app3 buildings pattern; `renderStyle=["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP","PICKING"]`). Two interchangeable colourings (length + noise-within-10m) = two knots on the same `roads` layer, both joins in one `roads_joined.json`, switched with the `TOGGLE_KNOT` widget. **Full-island load WITHOUT buildings is fast (~45 s)** (no per-building Python triangulation) — surface/water/parks/roads only; passing the island *polygon* to `OSM.load` clips roads to the island. ids/picking for water/parks/roads: generate `<layer>_ids.data` (all-zero local uint32, one per triangle, `ids:[start,size]` per feature) since `OSM.load` emits ids only for buildings+surface.
- **`knotOp`/`op` arithmetic is evaluated on the CPU, NOT in a shader**: the bundle does `operation.replaceAll("prevResult",...); eval(operation)` in JS. So UTK has **no user-programmable GPU compute path** — its only GPU-evaluated step is `SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP` mapping an already-known per-vertex scalar to colour in the fragment shader. A "compute geometric length entirely in shaders" requirement therefore can't be met by stock UTK; the faithful realisation is to compute the reduction in the Python data layer and let the GPU colour-map shader render it (document the trade-off, like "count within radius not expressible in grammar").
- **Browser OOM from OBJECTS-level plot knots on the buildings layer (app3)**: putting BOTH scatter axes (noise x + area y) as OBJECTS knots on the full-island `buildings` layer (~7.4M verts, 10141 comps) crashes the tab with the native "Out of Memory" page *while loading* (DevTools dies, no stack trace). Cause: at OBJECTS level the frontend expands a knot across EVERY vertex and, when building a LINKED plot, `attachPlots`→element-builder calls `getCoordsByLevel(OBJECTS)`/`getFunctionByLevel`/`getHighlightsByLevel` which each materialize an array-of-arrays totalling ~7.4M entries **per plot knot** (the per-vertex `coordinates` g[E] is even built then discarded — vega rows only use `_abstract`/`_index`/`_highlight`). One buildings knot ≈ app2's baseline; a SECOND buildings knot ~doubles those transient 7.4M structures → OOM. FIX: keep only ONE buildings knot (`noiseImpact`, OBJECTS) = map color + scatter x + CLICK-highlight (the plot click handler highlights *every* plot knot's element by index, so the building highlight comes from this knot — the y knot needn't be on buildings). Put the y axis (area) on a LIGHTWEIGHT helper layer: a `TRIANGLES_3D_LAYER` with one tiny 1 m triangle per building (3 verts, local indices `[0,1,2]`, `[start,size]` coords in doubles=i*9/9, indices=i*3/3) at the building centroid, carrying an OBJECTS area join (`areaTheme`→`areaPoints`). Emit components in `buildings.json` order so the LINKED merge (a POSITIONAL zip that **throws** "knots of a plot must have the same number of elements" if lengths differ) aligns row-for-row. The helper layer is referenced only by the non-map `areaAxis` knot but STILL loads, because the layer-load loop iterates ALL component knots' `out.name`s (`getKnots`, not just `map.knots`). ~30k verts vs 7.4M ⇒ negligible. Can't browser-verify OOM in this harness (no live GPU/DevTools), but the live server serves `/getLayer?layer=areaPoints` + all `/files/*` 200.
- **noise.csv** (app2) is a generic 5000-row 311 sample (only ~1051 Manhattan, many non-noise types like HEAT/HOT WATER); the prompt treats the whole file as "noise events". For 500 m radius counts, project events 4326→32618 and centroids 3395→32618 (UTM 18N, true meters — EPSG:3395 metric is distorted ~1.32× at 40.7° lat) and `KDTree.query_ball_point(r=500)`. # Manhattan Street Network — Streets of New York

A **fully browser-side** (no backend) web app that renders a map of Manhattan and
colours every road segment either by its **length** or by the **number of noise
events within a 10-metre radius**. Road metrics are computed in a distributed
fashion on the **GPU (WebGPU)** when available, with an automatic CPU fallback.

Built with [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/) + TypeScript and
[MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org/). OSM data comes live from the Overpass
API; noise data is loaded from a local CSV — everything runs in the browser.

---

## Features

| Requirement | How it is met |
|---|---|
| OSM base layers (surface, parks, water, roads) | One combined Overpass query over the `"Manhattan Island"` named area → `osmtogeojson` → four GeoJSON layers |
| Road length, distributed/GPU | WebGPU compute kernel (`one thread per road`) sums segment lengths in projected metres; CPU fallback if WebGPU is absent |
| Load noise CSV | `public/noise.csv` is fetched and parsed entirely in the browser |
| Count noise events ≤ 10 m of each segment | WebGPU compute kernel computes point-to-segment distance per road × event and counts hits ≤ 10 m (CPU fallback) |
| Colour by length **or** noise + toggle | "Length / Noise (10m)" buttons in the top-left panel switch the road colour ramp and legend live |
| Pick any layer element, colour changes on click | Click queries all four layers; the selected feature is highlighted yellow via MapLibre feature-state, and its attributes show in the info panel |
| Console logging | Every major step (fetch, parse, compute backend, spatial join, render, picks) logs to the browser console |

---

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js ≥ 18** and npm
- A modern browser. For GPU compute, use one with **WebGPU** (Chrome/Edge 113+).
  Without WebGPU the app still works using the CPU fallback.
- Internet access (Overpass API + OpenStreetMap raster tiles).

---

## The noise dataset

The app reads `public/noise.csv`, which is a copy of the task dataset at
`/home/lucas/projects/master-degree/autark-experiments/data/noise.csv`.
A copy already ships in this project. If you need to refresh it:

```bash
cp /home/lucas/projects/master-degree/autark-experiments/data/noise.csv public/noise.csv
```

Only the `Latitude` / `Longitude` columns are used; rows are filtered to a
Manhattan bounding box before the spatial join.

---

## Run it

```bash
# 1. install dependencies
npm install

# 2. start the dev server (http://localhost:3005)
npm run dev
```

Then open **http://localhost:3005** in your browser and open the DevTools
console to follow the progress logs.

### Production build / preview

```bash
npm run build      # tsc --noEmit + vite build  → dist/
npm run preview    # serve the built dist/ on http://localhost:3005
```

---

## How it works

1. **Map shell** — MapLibre GL initialises with a faint OSM raster basemap.
2. **Data load (parallel)** — a single Overpass query fetches roads + parks +
   water + landuse for *Manhattan Island* (with exponential backoff on HTTP
   429/504), while the noise CSV is loaded and parsed in the browser.
3. **Parse** — `osmtogeojson` converts the Overpass response; features are split
   into the `roads`, `parks`, `water` and `surface` layers.
4. **Projection** — road vertices and noise points are projected to a local
   equirectangular metre grid centred on Manhattan (so distances are in metres).
5. **Compute** — `src/compute/gpuCompute.ts` runs two WebGPU kernels:
   - **length**: per road, sum of its segment lengths.
   - **noise**: per road, count of noise events whose nearest distance to the
     road polyline is ≤ 10 m.
   If WebGPU is unavailable, `src/compute/cpuCompute.ts` produces identical
   results on the CPU. The chosen backend is logged to the console.
6. **Render** — roads are coloured by the active mode; surface/parks/water are
   filled. The legend and the "Length / Noise (10m)" toggle update together.
7. **Picking** — clicking anywhere queries all four layers; the top hit is
   highlighted yellow and its properties (including `road_length` and
   `noise_count`) are shown in the info panel.

---

## Project structure

```
index.html                  UI shell (map, controls, legend, info panel)
public/noise.csv            noise dataset (served browser-side)
src/
  main.ts                   orchestration + status/logging
  data/
    types.ts                shared types
    overpassClient.ts       single Overpass query + backoff
    osmParser.ts            Overpass JSON → 4 GeoJSON layers
    noiseLoader.ts          CSV fetch + parse + bbox filter
  compute/
    projection.ts           lon/lat → local metres
    gpuCompute.ts           WebGPU length + noise-count kernels
    cpuCompute.ts           CPU fallback (identical results)
    roadMetrics.ts          backend selection (GPU → CPU)
  map/
    mapManager.ts           MapLibre layers, toggle, picking, legend
    styles.ts               colour ramps + selection colour
```

---

## Notes & trade-offs

- **GPU "distributed" compute**: work is parallelised one thread per road
  segment via WebGPU compute shaders. The CPU fallback is provided so the app
  is usable in browsers without WebGPU; both paths yield the same numbers.
- **Projection**: a local equirectangular projection introduces < 0.3 % error
  over Manhattan — far below the 10 m radius precision required — and keeps the
  GPU kernels free of trigonometry.
- **Noise filtering**: the supplied CSV is a city-wide 311 sample; events are
  pre-filtered to a Manhattan bounding box so the spatial join stays bounded.
- **Overpass etiquette**: only **one** query is issued, over the
  `"Manhattan Island"` area, with exponential backoff on rate-limit responses.

```
    cpuCompute.ts           CPU fallback (identical results)
    roadMetrics.ts          backend selection (GPU → CPU)
  map/
    mapManager.ts           MapLibre layers, toggle, picking, legend
    styles.ts               colour ramps + selection colour
```

---

## Notes & trade-offs

- **GPU "distributed" compute**: work is parallelised one thread per road
  segment via WebGPU compute shaders. The CPU fallback is provided so the app
  is usable in browsers without WebGPU; both paths yield the same numbers.
- **Projection**: a local equirectangular projection introduces < 0.3 % error
  over Manhattan — far below the 10 m radius precision required — and keeps the
  GPU kernels free of trigonometry.
- **Noise filtering**: the supplied CSV is a city-wide 311 sample; events are
  pre-filtered to a Manhattan bounding box so the spatial join stays bounded.
- **Overpass etiquette**: only **one** query is issued, over the
  `"Manhattan Island"` area, with exponential backoff on rate-limit responses.
